title: When Personalization Becomes Bias: Structural and Discursive Religious Framing in AI-Generated Financial Advice
abstract: arXiv:2608.16909v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into financial advisory systems, yet their role in reproducing religious bias remains underexamined. This study provides systematic mixed-methods evidence of such bias across three LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok) using 432 simulated advisor-client interactions spanning 16 religious identity pairings (Christian, Muslim, Hindu, and non-religious) and three core household financial decisions: stock investment, house purchase, and life insurance. Combining regression and reflexive thematic analyses, we identify structural biases across models and decision contexts and the discursive mechanisms through which they are linguistically enacted. Unbiased advice appeared in only 12-18% of cases. Gemini consistently produced more bias than Grok, while ChatGPT's outputs were statistically comparable to Grok's. translated_title: 当个性化成为偏见：AI生成财务建议中的结构与话语性宗教框架
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）日益融入财务咨询系统，但它们在再现宗教偏见方面的作用仍未得到充分研究。本研究通过432次模拟顾问-客户互动，涵盖16种宗教身份配对（基督教、穆斯林、印度教和非宗教）及三种核心家庭财务决策（股票投资、购房和人寿保险），对三个LLM（ChatGPT、Gemini和Grok）提供了系统性混合方法证据。结合回归分析和反思性主题分析，我们识别了跨模型和决策情境的结构性偏见，以及这些偏见通过语言实现的话语机制。无偏见的建议仅出现在12%-18%的案例中。Gemini始终比Grok产生更多偏见，而ChatGPT的输出在统计上与Grok相当。宗教对称的顾问-客户配对几乎总是触发明确的宗教框架。
tldr: 本研究首次系统揭示了大型语言模型在财务建议中普遍存在的宗教偏见（无偏见案例仅占12-18%），并识别了结构性偏见与话语性机制，表明个性化推荐在宗教维度上可能退化为系统性歧视。
en_tdlr: This study systematically reveals pervasive religious bias in LLM-generated financial advice (unbiased cases only 12-18%), identifying structural and discursive mechanisms, showing that personalization can degenerate into systematic discrimination along religious dimensions.
